items.title: 66095_Benny Carter oral history interview
items.q: I said, 'Well, gee, this is done by Oliver Nelson --why don't you try to get him to come and do this segment for you.

ctx.x: And you saw all these people coming in? I mean, they came in while you were there. Did they -- did their work begin with one film, usually -- how did they break in? I mean, what was the process? Did they come there for one particular purpose -- with a contract already in their hands, or did they just come there and say, well, "Here I am. I'm gonna try to get some work in the studios."?
Well, I don't know about the others, but I know how Oliver Nelson came there, and I don't want to give any undue credit to myself, because it's not

why I'm telling you this, but when I was working at Universal, I was asked to look at a picture for a producer, and I looked at the picture and he said that he wanted a score like an album that he was going to play for me. And he played an album for me, and it was, I believe it was a Jimmy Smith album, that had been done by Oliver Nelson.
